dev:vita: the vita dev server, from anywhere
changeset: note a change of monolithium/utilities for the next release
check:agents: every AGENTS.md, skill and subagent within 150 lines, every link in them resolves
check:leaf-parity: every *.web.tsx / *.native.tsx leaf has its X.types.ts, and its partner where the package declares native
herdr: the pinned herdr with the repo's session and plugin (--reload new breadboard code, --stop)
herdr:install: the repo in your own herdr instead (e.g. Omarchy's): plugin, keys, the space Monocircuit/Platform
browser: the Chromium extension for a tab group per herdr space: install it, say how to load it
overview: live: worktrees, stacks, merge requests and issues (q quits, --worktree <dir> for one, --orchestration <name> for its issues and MRs)
changelog: the live view of what got into develop, by product and package: rewritten from GitLab and printed (--since 30d|2w|<date>, --watch: live, the tab changelog of the main space); not CHANGELOG.md
changelog:add: [--type <t>] [--area <a>] "<sentence>" an entry of this branch's MR for CHANGELOG.md, as .changelog/<issue>-<slug>.md
changelog:unreleased: what the next release's section of CHANGELOG.md would say, from .changelog/
changelog:release: <X.Y.Z> on the release branch: the fragments folded into CHANGELOG.md, vita's version set (skill release)
changelog:notes: <X.Y.Z> a release's section of CHANGELOG.md (the GitLab release's description)
changelog:check: every .changelog/ fragment valid; --mr: this MR adds one or carries no-changelog (CI check:changelog)
stack:up:
start the vita stack — of the worktree on --port

/ , else yours
stack:reset: throw away the data of that stack and set it up again
wt:new: <feature> a worktree on a new branch with its own stack (--shared, --fix, --origin <orchestration>)
wt:orchestrate: <name> <issue>… a space ⇶ <name> for this session, per issue a worktree with a briefed claude (--dry-run, --queue [--after !<mr>…]); <name> <issue> --to <agent> hands it to an idle agent (--after !<mr>…: once they are merged); <name> --title <text> what it shows instead of its name; <name> --end ends it once its worktrees are gone; <name> --changelog [--watch] its changelog
wt:plan: <name> [--work <n>…] [--merge <n>…] [--why <t>] the order of an orchestration's issues and merges, for its overview
wt:stack: give the worktree you are in its own stack
wt:check: lint, typecheck and test of what the branch changes (and what depends on it), cached; stamps the tree it passed: the pre-push hook refuses any other commit
wt:mr: open the draft MR of this worktree (--update sends the description again)
wt:note: <issue> --message-file <f> comment a file on an issue
wt:tick: [<issue>] [<box>…] the boxes of the issue, numbered; ticks the given ones
wt:action: <kind> <text> [--url <u> | --run <cmd>] ask the human for merge, try (opens the spot to check), decide (a question, --option per consequence, --recommend <option>), plan or look: a row in ACTIONS of the orchestration's overview (--list, --done <id>, --orchestration <name> for the orchestrator); change <what>: a change for the MR, draft at once and its merge withdrawn (--mr !N with --orchestration)
wt:wait: !<mr>… [--then "<what>"] run in the background: ends with the line to go on with once the MRs are merged (early when one is closed or stays in conflict, after --hours, default 8); the overview shows the wait (--cancel)
wt:issues: issues of merged MRs nobody commented on since the merge
wt:prune: close worktrees and branches of merged MRs (--dry-run)
wt:herdr: herdr: root and overview, a space per worktree, tabs of running stacks; after a restart it all runs again
wt:remove: <feature> stack, worktree and merged branch away

products/vita/web.commands: this list: vita first, then the root
products/vita/web.overview: live: worktrees, stacks, merge requests and issues (q quits)
products/vita/web.dev: the app on the port of this worktree, logged in
products/vita/web.dev:ready: [<route>…] wait until pnpm dev answers and has built these pages (default /editor)
products/vita/web.dev:setup: stack up, migrate, bucket, Keycloak, seed — a fresh stack in one go
products/vita/web.dev:webpack: the app with webpack instead of turbopack
products/vita/web.dev:cpu: the app with a CPU profile
products/vita/web.logs: [<path>…] what the browser's devtools logger wrote: entries, --state <name>, --paths, --since 2m
products/vita/web.build:cpu: production build with a CPU profile
products/vita/web.build:migrate: bundle the migration runner for the image
products/vita/web.stack:up: start Postgres, Keycloak and SeaweedFS of this checkout
products/vita/web.stack:down: stop the containers of this checkout, data stays
products/vita/web.stack:reset: throw away the data of this checkout and set it up again
products/vita/web.routes:generate: the page.tsx files from core's route table (--check: only compare, CI check:routes)
products/vita/web.pg:generate: generate a migration from src/server/db/schema.ts (skill db-migration)
products/vita/web.pg:seed: fill the database with the dev data
products/vita/web.pg:visualizer: the schema as a diagram, on the port of this worktree
products/vita/web.startup-images: the iOS launch screens per device, light and dark, from the logo
products/vita/web.screenshots:manifest: the install dialog's screenshots of the atlas, from pnpm dev (Chromium)
products/vita/web.keycloak:setup: the MCP clients, their scopes and the login theme in Keycloak
products/vita/web.test:coverage: unit tests with coverage (CI has a floor)
products/vita/web.test:int: the operations against the real Postgres and object storage

packages/monolithium.check-contrast: contrast check of the built Storybook
packages/monolithium.tokens: write tokens.css and theme.css from src/tokens/tokens.ts

packages/breadboard.lint: ESLint of what stays JavaScript, cargo fmt and clippy
packages/breadboard.lint:rs: cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings of the Rust breadboard
packages/breadboard.test: node --test (the nvim Lua in a headless nvim) and cargo test
packages/breadboard.test:rs: cargo test of the Rust breadboard

packages/breadboard-gauntlet.snap: a screenshot (text, PNG) of any TUI in a pty, in a gauntlet world: for the rewrite's critics
packages/breadboard-gauntlet.gauntlet: the black-box suite: breadboard in a pty against a recorded world (this checkout's binary; BREADBOARD_SUBJECT: another)

packages/eslint-config.build:prod: build the configs as the hooks and CI load them
packages/eslint-config.test: the platform rules on fixtures (build:prod first)
